findings.title: Bench RSS delta covers unrelated runtimes
findings.why_it_matters: rss_before is captured before all 6 benchmark runtimes (plain+keyed at 1x/2x/4x), while rss_after is divided by the dedicated sample live count only (n). Delta therefore covers ~15n facts of allocator high-water that is never returned, inflating bytes_per_fact ~15x and making mode comparisons meaningless; #15 fixed only the after side (sample kept alive to line 339) but left the before side misplaced.

findings.suggested_fix: Index the second phase by (subject, relation) or premise event via horns_by_premise/facts_by_relation so only behaviors whose body could mention the dead premise are re-checked; or record reverse premise edges at fire time.
findings.title: Retract path scans all live behaviors per trigger
findings.why_it_matters: After the indexed direct-children phase, every retract/correct still clones and walks the full live_behaviors vector with horn_body_matches_except per entry. N retracts over D live derived is O(N*D); retract_examine bumps per live behavior so instrumented tests will show linear examine counts per retract, the same cliff shape as the original full-log scan at smaller constant.

findings.suggested_fix: Make premise discovery overlap-aware instead of point-gated: collect candidate premise facts whose VT overlaps the trigger window (valid_from < trigger_to and valid_to > trigger_from, with None as +inf) and conjunct each candidate window, rather than only facts live at trigger valid_from. At minimum, retry search at each distinct candidate valid_from within the trigger window or iterate all overlapping combinations.
findings.title: Horn discovery misses late-starting premise overlap
findings.why_it_matters: Multi-premise Horn discovery is point-gated on the trigger valid_from, so an overlapping premise that starts later is never found and the conjoined head is silently missed, order-dependently. Concrete: register two-premise relatedTo rule; Assert AB [2015,2020) first; Assert BC trigger [2010,None) second. At the BC trigger, search_at filters other premises via live_facts_for_relation(rel, MAX, vt=2010) (eval.rs:619), and AB [2015,2020) is not live at vt=2010, so search returns None and no AC head is emitted even though the conjunction [2015,2020) is non-empty. Reverse insertion order (BC first, AB trigger at 2015 with BC live at 2015) does derive [2015,2020). Same logical state yields different derived sets depending on insertion order; as_of misses the derived triple in one order.

findings.title: Scalar or missing steps yield vacuous OK check
findings.trigger: A check row with `steps: [just-a-string]`, `steps: not-a-list`, or a missing `steps:` key (scalar-row typo of the #23 class, or forgotten key), then `kutha-gov precommit --check <id>` or `json --check <id>`.
findings.why_it_matters: Named-check OK with zero executed steps is the textbook silent pass; the --check subset surfaces report it without any hint that the check is vacuous. Consequence: DictCheck holds zero steps; run() iterates nothing and returns a finding-free result that prints `OK <id>` / `"passed": true` while zero oracles ran. Mitigating backstop (not a fix): full `selftest` classifies the stepless check UNPROVEN (selftest.py:323-324) and fails red — unless the row also carries a selftest.skip reason, in which case it SKIP-passes having run nothing.

findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the nameless handling: collect non-mapping rows into a LoadError alongside survivors (fail closed, keep valid checks per #20 precedent), plus a test_selftest.py-style oracle (valid rows survive + HIGH present).
findings.title: Scalar rows in checks.yaml silently skipped
findings.trigger: Append `- just-a-string` (or `42`) under `checks:` in .kutha/dictionaries/checks.yaml, then run `kutha-gov precommit`, `ci`, `json`, `selftest`, or `list`.
findings.why_it_matters: Governor constitution claims fail-closed dictionary handling (META.md unknown-kind HIGH, CE #20 nameless-row LoadError). Scalar rows evade every surface: the config mistake is invisible exactly where the governor is supposed to catch config mistakes. Consequence: Loader `continue`s silently: no LoadErrorCheck, no HIGH from any check (no dictionary self-structure oracle exists — checks.yaml has require_fields/unique for invariants/bridges/honeycomb rows but none for select checks), `list` hides the row, full `ci` stays green while the malformed row never ran. Same silent-filter class as prior #23, which was fixed for the test matrix but never reached the governor dictionary. Loader code unchanged since before dd38c95 (diff empty), but dictionary.py is explicitly in this review's scope.

findings.suggested_fix: Track seen ids in get_checks; on duplicate, keep-first plus LoadErrorCheck naming the dup id (fail closed, survivors keep running). Add an oracle (duplicate-id row → HIGH load) and consider a dictionary self-check `unique: id` on select checks.
findings.title: Duplicate check ids silently overwrite
findings.trigger: Duplicate an existing check id in checks.yaml (e.g. second `id: docs-entry` row with weaker steps, via bad merge or edit), then run any surface including full `kutha-gov ci`.
findings.why_it_matters: A duplicated id permanently retires the original check's oracles with zero signal on any surface; diff review is the only backstop for a fail-closed governor. Consequence: Last row silently overwrites the first in the loader dict: the stronger check's oracles never run, everything prints OK/green, and no oracle fires — no `unique: id` / require_fields check exists on select checks (the invariants-ledger step at checks.yaml:986-994 only cross-refs ids into ledgers, never uniqueness), and selftest proves only the surviving row.

Rule-pin gating is also point-based (live_horns filters pin live at trigger valid_from), so a pin whose window starts after the trigger start is skipped even though the three-way conjunction is non-empty; typically masked because pins are open-ended.
